name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 19, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:01 p.m., on January 19, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 14, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 6:06 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Chery Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that staff would like to remove Item CS1 and re-calendar the
matter for another meeting.

Mayor Schlicht noted that she would like the opportunity to discuss Item CS1 if possible.

Attorney Curley said that the matter can remain on the agenda as long as the discussion is within
parameters of giving staff direction towards setting price and terms.

City Council Minutes  1  January 19, 2015
 CS1. Conference With Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Property: That Portion of Oso Creek Trail System Owned by American Golf
  (The Open Space Located Between Casta Del Sol Road and Jeronimo Road - The
  Tennis Pavilion to the West and the Casta Del Sol Residential Community to the
  East.) City Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg and Assistant City Manager
  Keith Rattay. Owner’s Negotiators: American Golf President. Under Negotiation:
  Price and Terms.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel-Anticipated Litigation. Significant exposure to
  litigation pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: one
  case.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Schlicht recessed the meeting to closed session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that the Council considered price and terms for item CS1 and
there will be further open-session discussion under agenda item 19. For Item CS2, the Council
received an update and gave direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Schlicht

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  South Orange County Economic Coalition Introduction and Release of First South
  Orange County Economic Report

  Chairman Duane Cave made a presentation to the City Council on the South Orange
  County Economic Coalition and invited the Council Members to two upcoming events.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jim Leach, Santa Margarita Water District (SMWD): announced that SMWD is proposing changes
to its rates to take effect in March. They will be hosting a number of public information session
with one in Mission Viejo on February 10, 2015, from 6:00 to 7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community
Center. The actual public hearing will be held on March 4, 2015, at 7:00 p.m. at the SMWD office.

Dan Avery, M.V.: asked the City to stop thinking in terms of government when spending on the
arts and to categorize appropriately. He stated that the arts educate and shape souls and he asked
the Council to consider the continued funding of the summer Pacific Symphony concert.

City Council Minutes  2  January 19, 2015
 Jim Montrella, M.V.: stated that he is proud of previous Councils and the decisions that were made
with the Nadadores. He expressed concern that infrastructure will not be maintained and he said
that the City's greatest assets are its citizens, youth, and seniors and there should be programs for
all. Mr. Montrella stated that he hopes that he can look back in 6-10 years and say this City Council
did a great job just like the previous ones.

Chuck McCullough and Scot Shier, Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce: Mr. McCullough
announced that he will begin attending the first City Council Meeting of every month to announce
what is going on at the Chamber. Mr. Shier encouraged the City Council Members to attend the
Chamber's meetings and to connect with the business community. He announced that the next
ribbon cutting is on January 30 at Evolution Swim Academy and the Chamber’s monthly mixer is
February 19 at the Pizza Studio.

Stephen Wontrbski, M.V.: stated that he recognizes a recurrent theme from staff who refrain from
following Council Members suggestions or one from a member of the public regarding a cost
cutting idea. He stated that staff's comments are negative and it is rare that they agree to explore
an idea or get back to the Council or public with a study.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 12, and 13 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated December 12, 2014 in the Amount of $2,702,648.69

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated December 19, 2014 in the Amount of $1,642,269.11

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated December 24, 2014 in the Amount of $719,979.86
City Council Minutes  3  January 19, 2015
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Fiscal Year 2013-14 Mission Viejo Housing Authority Annual Report

  Received and filed.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2014

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2014

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  November 2014

  Received and filed.

10.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for November 2014

  Received and filed.

11.  Ninety-day follow-up on cost associated with City’s Permit Fee Waiver Program for
  Water Conservation Improvements.

  Directed staff to continue to market and implement the Permit Fee Waiver Program for
  Water Conservation Improvements, with no Budget Amendment at this time.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Mayor Schlicht announced that she apologized to Planning Commissioner Julia Malisos
  for voting no on her appointment to the Commission. Mayor Schlicht stated that Ms.
  Malisos is one of the most qualified people to be on the Planning Commission and her no
  vote was in error. She also announced that she will be submitting Larry Gilbert's
  qualifications for the Oversight Board to the City Clerk for the public record.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
  Minutes for the regular meeting of January 5, 2015, as presented.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  4  January 19, 2015
 12.  Laguna Niguel/Mission Viejo Commuter Rail Station Improvements

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht noted that there will not be any general fund tax dollars supporting this
  project.

  Director Chagnon confirmed that the project will be entirely funded by OCTA and may
  actually lower the City's annual maintenance costs.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) No. C-4-1784 between Orange County
  Transportation Authority and cities of Laguna Niguel and Mission Viejo for Laguna
  Niguel/Mission Viejo Station Improvements.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  Addition and Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Member Sachs expressed concern with the wording in the second paragraph of the
  policy.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 15-04, as amended, Providing for the Establishment of and Revisions to select
  Personnel Policies (remove the 2nd paragraph of the "Policy" section of the smoking policy
  per second motion below.)

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to remove
  the 2nd paragraph of the Policy section in the Smoking Policy.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  January 19, 2015
 NEW BUSINESS

18.  Landscape Slope Along Country Club Drive

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in favor of the city assuming responsibility for maintenance of slopes
  behind Bodega Lane: Christine Saracino, M.V.; Dawn Vukich, M.V.; Hweimin Wang
  M.V.; Randy Raus (speaking on behalf of Val Buena,) M.V.; Darrin Mourer, M.V.; Carl
  Schwab, M.V.; Sandra Hasen, M.V.; Robert Brum, M.V.; and George Erickson, M.V.

  The following presented written statements in favor of the City assuming landscape
  maintenance responsibility for the area in question: Christopher and Monique Risoon,
  M.V.; Dan Davari, M.V.; Hweimin Wang, M.V.; Stephanie McCarron, M.V.; Gina
  Connoy, M.V.; and Andrew McCarron, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to work
  with the homeowners to adjust the landscape and irrigation to provide a consistent
  landscape look along Country Club Drive.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  By consensus, the City Council requested that staff develop some criteria for taking over
  landscape areas.

RECESS

At the hour of 7:27 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:42
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

OLD BUSINESS

14.  Revised Community Services Master Plan

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented staff report.

  Robert David Breton, M.V.: announced that he is a prior Chairman of the Community
  Services Commission and he worked on this Master Plan. The proposed Master Plan is
  intended as a valuable resource tool and guide for future planning for the optimum delivery
  of recreational and cultural activities. It is built on solid foundations and there are
  objectives with ways to implement goals and policies.

City Council Minutes  6  January 19, 2015
   Ron Ruef, Community Services Commission Chairman, M.V.: stated that the Master Plan
  will help build upon the plan that was laid before the City by predecessors and to address
  changing demographics and needs of the residents. The Community Services Commission
  worked on it for several years with public forums, surveys and community workshops and
  he asked for the City Council's approval.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve the Community Services Master Plan as recommended by the Community
  Services Commission.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to call for the
  question.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, MAIN MOTION carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

15.  Park Restroom Master Plan

  Council Member Ury distributed a map for the Council to reference during the discussion.

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the Park
  Restroom Master Plan as recommended by the Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

16.  Pre-Budget Discussion Workshop

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the budget meeting last week was very encouraging
  and a lot was accomplished. He asked why the City can't give a rebate to the taxpayers and
  he asked the Council to give staff direction to implement cost savings.

City Council Minutes  7  January 19, 2015
   By consensus, the City Council Members placed park restrooms after playground
  renovations on the priority list that was developed at the budget workshop and directed
  staff to budget for two park restrooms in the upcoming budget.

RECESS

At the hour of 7:27 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

NEW BUSINESS (Continued)

17.  Revised Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Public Service Grant
  Application Rating Criteria.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to adopt Resolution
  15-05, Adopting an Amendment of Funding Criteria for Award of Community
  Development Block Grant Funds to Non-Profit Public Service Organizations and
  Amending the City council Policy Manual.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

19.  Oso Creek Trail and Open Space

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff
  report.

  Bruce Teel, M.V.: stated that he is not in favor of the City purchasing the property and
  that he like the rustic part of the trail.

  Carole Weidler, M.V.: stated that the Casta del Sol residents she spoke to today asked that
  the Council please take action to improve the looks of the area as it is an eyesore to guests
  and residents entering Casta del Sol.

  The following presented a written comment in favor of improving that part of Oso Creek
  Trail: Andrew and Sylvia Hoffart, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to direct staff to
  write a letter recognizing the offer and rejecting the opportunity to purchase the parcels.

City Council Minutes  8  January 19, 2015
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  By consensus, the City Council directed that staff should reemphasize the City's desire for
  an easement.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

20.  Appointment to the Investment Advisory Commission

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  appoint Victoria Avery to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

21.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCFA
  Board of Directors.

22.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented the report.

23.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that there is no San Joaquin Hills TCA Board Meeting
  in January.

24.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

25.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  9  January 19, 2015
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked Mayor Schlicht for apologizing to Commissioner Julia
Malisos both at the Planning and Transportation Commission meeting and earlier tonight. She
outlined her attendance at the Chamber of Commerce event and the City's budget workshop last
week. She also visited Pavion Park and when she was there, there were about 150 people at the
park. She encouraged residents to go visit the park as it is something to behold. There are swings
that hold wheelchairs and kids of all different ages, skills and disabilities can use it. Council
Member Bucknum announced that the City Council will be honoring the Mission Viejo High
School and Trabuco Hills High School bands for taking home medals in their respective categories
in the state competition. She announced that for the second year in a row, Southern California
Swimming has named Coach Bill Rose of the Nadadores as Coach of the Year. She asked her
colleagues if the Council can honor Coach Rose at a meeting in February. Council Member
Bucknum concluded with a quote from Martin Luther King, Jr.: "The function of education is to
teach one to think intensively and to think critically. Intelligence plus character; that is the goal of
true education."

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs asked that this Council be given a chance to come together and work on
behalf of the City and the City's best interests. He stated that some of the requests that are being
made of the Council need a little time to be vetted. It is a different Council and they have taken
up some things quite readily and quickly. Council Member Sachs announced that he too visited
Pavion Park and there were tons of kids there having fun. He stated that it is a really neat park and
the City should be very proud to see the amount of participation there.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury asked if Mayor Schlicht will be able to attend the City Selection Committee
meeting on Friday and if not, can she designate an alternate.

Mayor Schlicht announced that she has designated Council Member Sachs to attend and vote on
behalf of the City.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked Sheriff Sandra Hutchens who visited last week and gave he and
Council Member Sachs a briefing on her department. He also did a five hour ride-along with a
Deputy and he noted that they didn't find any crime or speeding but they did pull over a Prius
driver for a broken tail light. Mayor Pro Tem Raths said that Lt. Brad NewMyer and his deputies
are doing a good job. He also thanked Recreation Director Mark Nix for the tour of the parks and
facilities. He stated that this is a very happy City and he has enjoyed his first 50 days on the
Council.
City Council Minutes  10  January 19, 2015
 Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht stated that she is so pleased to see the community coming back out to the
podium. It has always been her belief that we get better government through public participation
and she thanked residents for making the effort and doing their civic duty. In closing, she quoted
Todd Spitzer: "The reason we have elections is to change public policy."

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:23 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, February 2, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 2, 2015

City Council Minutes  11  January 19, 2015
